In [[mathematics]], the '''centered icosahedral numbers''' also known as '''cuboctahedral numbers''' are a sequence of numbers, describing two different representations for these numbers as three-dimensional [[figurate number]]s. As centered icosahedral numbers, they are [[centered number]]s representing points arranged in the shape of a [[regular icosahedron]]. As cuboctahedral numbers, they represent points arranged in the shape of a [[cuboctahedron]], and are a [[Magic number (chemistry)|magic number]] for the [[face-centered cubic lattice]]. The centered icosahedral number for a specific <math>n</math> is given by <math display=block>\frac{(2n+1)\left(5n^2+5n+3\right)}{3}.</math>

The first such numbers are

{{bi|left=1.6|1, 13, 55, 147, 309, 561, 923, 1415, 2057, 2869, 3871, 5083, 6525, 8217, ... {{OEIS|A005902}}.}}
